title: Set 290

sentences.ko: 매니저가 나보고 새 팀을 맡으래. 좋은 일이긴 한데, 지난주까지 친구였던 사람들 위에서 상사 노릇을 하게 되는 거잖아. 거절하면 다시는 기회를 안 줄 것 같고, 하겠다고 하면 다 달라질까 봐 좀 걱정돼. 솔직히 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠어.
sentences.text: So my manager wants me to lead the new team, which is great, but I'd basically be the boss of people who were my friends last week. And if I say no, I don't think they'll ask me again, but if I say yes, I'm kind of worried it'll change everything. I honestly don't know what to do.

alts.text: My manager wants me running the new team. Great, right? Except I'd pretty much be bossing around people who were my buddies last week. If I turn it down, they probably won't ask again, but if I take it, I'm kinda scared it'll change everything. I seriously don't know what to do.

My manager would like me to lead the new team, which is wonderful, but I would essentially be supervising people who were my friends only last week. If I decline, I do not believe they will offer it again, yet if I accept, I am somewhat concerned that it will change everything. I truly do not know what to do.

sentences.note: **which is great, but** 은 앞에 한 말을 받아서 좋긴 한데 하고 걸리는 점을 붙일 때 씁니다. **turn it down** 은 제안을 거절한다는 뜻으로, say no 보다 조금 부드럽게 들립니다.
sentences.situation: 친구한테 고민 상담하면서 결론은 못 내리기

sentences.ko: 잠깐, 우리 얼마 만이지, 한 2년 됐나? 아직 시내에 있는 그 회사 다녀? 아니면 맨날 그만둔다더니 드디어 그만뒀어?
sentences.text: Wait, how long has it been, like two years? Are you still at that place downtown, or did you finally quit like you kept saying you would?

alts.text: Hold on, it's been what, two years? You still at that downtown place, or did you finally quit like you kept saying?
How long has it been, about two years? Are you still working at that company downtown, or did you eventually resign as you had often said you would?

sentences.note: **how long has it been** 은 오랜만에 만났을 때 이게 얼마 만이야 하고 반가워하는 말입니다. **like you kept saying you would** 는 너가 계속 그러겠다고 하던 것처럼이라는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 부엌 싱크대 고치는 영상 하나만 보려고 유튜브를 켰는데, 어쩌다 보니 어떤 아저씨가 낡은 배 고치는 걸 한 세 시간 동안 보고 있더라. 근데 싱크대는 아직도 물이 새. 정작 보려던 건 하나도 못 배운 거지.
sentences.text: I opened YouTube to watch one video on how to fix the kitchen sink, and somehow I ended up watching some guy restore an old boat for like three hours. And the sink's still leaking, so I didn't even learn the one thing I went on there for.

alts.text: I went on YouTube for one video on fixing the kitchen sink, and next thing I know I've spent like three hours watching some guy restore an old boat. Sink's still leaking, too, so I didn't even learn the one thing I was there for.

I opened YouTube to watch a single video on repairing the kitchen sink, and somehow I spent about three hours watching a man restore an old boat. The sink is still leaking, so I did not even learn the one thing I had gone there to find.

sentences.note: **ended up** 은 의도하지 않았는데 결국 그렇게 되어 버렸다는 뜻입니다. **went on there for** 는 거기 들어간 목적을 말할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 유튜브 보다가 시간 다 날린 얘기

sentences.ko: 일주일 내내 폰이 진짜 이상해. 배터리가 한 60에서 몇 분 만에 0이 되는데, 충전기를 꽂으면 다시 50이라고 떠. 그래서 진짜로 꺼질지 안 꺼질지 도무지 알 수가 없어.
sentences.text: My phone's been acting really weird all week. The battery goes from like sixty to zero in a few minutes, but then when I plug it in, it says it's back at fifty, so I never know if it's actually going to die on me.

alts.text: My phone's been super weird all week. Battery drops from like sixty to zero in a few minutes, then I plug it in and it says fifty, so I've got no clue if it's actually gonna die on me.

My phone has been behaving very strangely all week. The battery falls from about sixty percent to zero within a few minutes, but when I plug it in, it shows fifty percent again, so I can never tell whether it is actually going to shut down.

sentences.note: **acting really weird** 는 기계나 사람이 평소와 다르게 이상하게 군다는 뜻입니다. **die on me** 는 쓰고 있는데 하필 꺼져 버린다는 느낌으로, 배터리나 차가 갑자기 멈출 때 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 너가 말해 준 태국 음식점 드디어 가 봤는데, 커리는 진짜 너 말이 딱 맞더라. 근데 자리 나는 데 거의 한 시간을 기다려서, 다시 가면 그냥 포장해 올 것 같아.
sentences.text: We finally tried that Thai place you told me about, and you were totally right about the curry. But we waited almost an hour for a table, so if we go back, I think we're just getting takeout.

alts.text: We finally hit up that Thai place you mentioned, and dude, that curry? You weren't kidding. But we waited almost an hour for a table, so next time it's just takeout.

We finally visited the Thai restaurant you recommended, and you were entirely correct about the curry. However, we waited nearly an hour for a table, so if we return, I believe we will simply order takeout.

sentences.note: **you were totally right about** 은 그건 네 말이 완전 맞았다고 인정할 때 씁니다. **getting takeout** 은 음식을 포장해 간다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 추천한 식당 다녀와서 후기 말하기

reviewed: 1번 casual 의 mess everything up 은 망친다는 뜻이라 원문의 다 달라진다(change everything)보다 세졌다. change everything 으로 맞췄다
1번 note 의 say no 와 함께 아주 자주 쓴다는 설명이 어색해서 say no 보다 조금 부드러운 말이라고 고쳤다
2번 casual 의 or'd you 는 글로 적으면 알아보기 어려운 축약이라 or did you 로 고쳤다
3번 한국어 들어간 이유였던 딱 하나도 못 배운 거지 는 번역투라 정작 보려던 건 하나도 못 배운 거지 로 고쳤다
4번 note 의 acting weird 는 문장에 그대로 나오지 않는다(acting really weird). 문장에 있는 그대로 짚게 고쳤다
5번 casual 의 you nailed it on the curry 는 추천이 맞았다는 뜻으로는 어색한 쓰임이다. that curry? You weren't kidding 으로 바꿨다
